model_card.inputs: 17 keypoints + person box from YOLO26n-pose + ByteTrack (no video stored; face points only as head position)
model_card.windows: last 2 s at 10 fps, scored every 0.5 s; torso-scaled, pair-centred
model_card.classifier: ensemble: average of LightGBM (36 features incl. body-relative limb speed, path straightness, rhythm, impacts) and a 78k-parameter 1D-CNN over the active pair's keypoints (pair-centred and body-centred); fast non-violent windows weighted 4x as hard negatives
model_card.split: 15% of groups locked as a hold-out (stratified by dataset and kind) and evaluated once; tuning by GroupKFold on the other 85%; AIRTLab camera pairs kept together
model_card.threshold: alarm when the smoothed score (alpha 0.6) stays >= 0.5054 for 1 s with 2+ people tracked; FIGHT_AT fixed on the training part at 9% normal-clip false alarms
failure_modes: hugs and close contact: 3 of 18 hold-out hug/clap clips raised an alarm
fast group movement with contact (sports, play) still alarms more often than calm scenes
alarms usually come 1.5-2.5 s after a fight starts on our own videos: early warning is not shown yet
impacts are rarely detected at 10 fps (collision features are weak)
operating range: camera about one floor up, people at least ~60 px tall, not wide crowd views
a fight with only one person tracked can't raise FIGHT

disclosure: Official numbers are from a third look at a hold-out of 470 clips (also used for v4 and v5). Own-camera numbers come from 7 short videos (leave one video out). Dataset clips are 2-5 s long, so false alarms per camera-hour are not measured yet; live-room numbers come from our own labelled footage. Practice-run lesson: 100% on KTH, zero live until retuned. We detect physical aggression from body motion only; we do not claim verbal or online bullying, weapon recognition, or night vision.
